subject: URGENT: BrightCart hosted chat — live degradation during peak
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@brightcart.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCart Ops <ops@brightcart.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T16:58:00Z
Subject: Severe p99 spike on hosted streaming during FlashSale window

Hi Jonas —

We're seeing dramatic p99 latency spikes on the hosted streaming chat endpoint between 16:45-17:05 PT during our FlashSale peak. Customers are reporting session stalls (SSE connections dropping) and several support tickets popped up in the last 10 minutes. Attached is a quick screenshot of the p95/p99 graph and a short tail of logs from one instance.

Impact: ~8% of sessions hitting >2.5s token latency (p99), some reconnect storms. This is hitting our conversion funnel. We need immediate mitigation and ETA on fix.

Samir
VP Product, BrightCart

Attachments: brightcart-p99-graph-20280614.png, streaming-tail-logs.txt
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T17:03:12Z
Subject: FWD: Severe p99 spike on hosted streaming during FlashSale window

Forwarding from BrightCart — high priority customer impact for hosted streaming (SSE/WebSocket) during a peak event. Key asks:
- Immediate mitigation to stabilize sessions (reduce p99)
- Short public statement we can give BrightCart in 30m
- Root cause triage cadence and exec brief if this escalates

Quick context: BrightCart is on a medium-size reserved plan but using hosted streaming paths. Samir attached graphs — looks like tail latency and reconnection churn.

Please escalate to infra and ops. Dev/Marcus, propose a 15m mitigation (below) and confirm risks.

Proposed quick mitigations (open to alternatives):
- Temporarily route BrightCart to a dedicated model variant / increase concurrency limit for their API key
- Bump streaming autoscaler floor for the affected shard(s) and freeze scale-down for 30m
- If needed, toggle a graceful fallback to non-streaming long-poll for web clients (we can throttle non-essential traffic)

I have looped in Grace for CS comms. I will call on any exec escalation if we can’t bring p99 down within 30m.

-Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-mitigation-checklist.md
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops-oncall@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T17:11:45Z
Subject: Re: FWD: Severe p99 spike on hosted streaming during FlashSale window

Jonas — triage notes from quick look:

- What we see: sharp connection churn aligned with increased token generation bursts (many short sessions with aggressive sampling). Worker-side CPU and NVMe IO are fine, but we see long tail in the runtime scheduler for some L3 kernels (likely KV-cache fragmentation + cold prefix lookups).
- Also saw spikes in connection resets originating from the gateway layer (we suspect an intermittent throttle on the streaming proxy when queue length crosses threshold).

Immediate mitigations I can roll (request approval to execute now):
1) Increase autoscaler min replicas from 6 -> 10 for the affected pool (will add ~8 GPUs to the pool). Estimated change propagation: 90s to boot new nodes plus warmup.
2) Apply aggressive prefix cache warmup for BrightCart model key (hot-cache prefetch).
3) Temporarily increase per-key concurrency and move their key to the dedicated hot-path routing (no model swap).

Risks: 1) cost spike while extra capacity is running; 2) small risk of transient errors during route switch (~1-2% error window).

I recommend we do 1+2 now, then 3 if p99 doesn't improve in 10 minutes. If Jonas approves, I'll coordinate with oncall to do the scale-up and prefetch.

-Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops-oncall@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T17:18:01Z
Subject: Re: FWD: Severe p99 spike on hosted streaming during FlashSale window

Adding ops perspective / quick playbook:
- I'll open an incident in our Jira/ops board and tag infra. Priority: Sev2 -> escalate to infra lead if not resolved in 20m.
- Hot fixes we can apply in parallel: 
  * Apply short-term client-side throttles by tier (drop non-authenticated polling to preserve capacity)
  * Increase streaming proxy queue threshold so it doesn't start failing connections when backpressure spikes (we will monitor queue latency)
  * Enable prefix-KV aggressive eviction guard to reduce fragmentation churn

I'll coordinate the scale-up with Dev. If scaling doesn't show improvement in 10m, we can fail back customer to poll-mode (non-streaming) while we investigate deeper.

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@brightcart.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Samir — first, sorry for the disruption. We have ops and infra working on an immediate mitigation plan and expect to have an initial stabilization within ~20 minutes.

What we'll deliver in the next 30 minutes:
- Stabilization actions (scale-up + cache warmup) kicked off (Jonas & Dev are on it)
- Dedicated status updates at +10m and +30m in this thread
- Post-incident follow-up: detailed RCA, performance regression analysis, and proposed credits if SLA thresholds hit

We will also proactively check your remaining promotional windows and coordinate to reduce additional traffic pressure if that helps. I will be your point for communications; feel free to escalate to me directly if anything changes.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
